newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money slightly firmer at 2.98/3.00 pct.
newsitem.headline: German call money slightly firmer at 2.98/3.00 pct.

text.p: German call money rates were slightly firmer at 2.98/3.00 percent in midday trade on Thursday compared with 2.95/3.00 percent on Wednesday as bank reserves at the Bundesbank were lower.

Traders expected rates to remain slightly below the Bundesbank's fixed-rate repo level of 3.00 percent ahead of the weekend amid views there was ample liquidity in the market despite the drop in reserves.
But rates could begin to inch higher on Monday when the Bundesbank sets the minimum reserve level for June, which is expected to be about 41.1 billion marks.
"It doesn't really matter these days what the level of reserves is during the month until we get the minimum reserve level and then see how the market looks," said one trader.
Commercial bank reserves fell to 39.9 billion marks as of Wednesday from 41.1 billion marks on Tuesday, while the monthly average remained steady at 40.3 billion marks.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average on Thursday FIONA was at 3.01800 percent from 3.01600 percent on Wednesday.
